steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Glycolysis: glucose -> 2 pyruvate (cytoplasm); net 2 ATP, 2 NADH; Link: pyruvate -> acetyl CoA + CO₂ + NADH (mito matrix); Krebs: acetyl CoA + 3NAD⁺ + FAD + GDP -> 2CO₂ + 3NADH + FADH₂ + GTP; ETC: NADH/FADH₂ -> H⁺ gradient -> ATP synthase -> ATP

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: SLP: direct phosphate transfer (glycolysis, Krebs); OxPhos: H⁺ pumped across inner membrane, flow through ATP synthase

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Theoretical: 10 NADH (2.5 each) + 2 FADH₂ (1.5 each) + 4 ATP = 32 ATP; Actual ~30-32

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Anaerobic: animals: pyruvate + NADH -> lactate + NAD⁺ (lactate dehydrogenase); Yeast: pyruvate -> acetaldehyde + CO₂ -> ethanol + NAD⁺

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Q: Calculate total ATP from one glucose via aerobic respiration. Explain why yield is often less than theoretical --- Solution: Glycolysis: 2 ATP + 2 NADH (3-5 ATP); Link: 2 NADH (5 ATP); Krebs: 2 ATP + 6 NADH (15 ATP) + 2 FADH₂ (3 ATP) = 25-30 + 4 = 29-32 ATP. Less because: proton leak, shuttle costs (glycerol-3-P shuttle vs malate-aspartate), ATP for transport
